title: Capital Gains — Transfer, Computation, Exemptions and Loss Set-off

content.overview: Capital gains are computed as the full value of consideration less the cost of acquisition, cost of improvement and expenditure on transfer. The result is short-term or long-term by holding period. Exemptions require the reinvestment the exemption section states. A loss is set off only as the set-off section allows. Computation comes before exemption. An exemption is lost if the new asset is not acquired as required.

cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.

enhancement.definition: Capital gains are computed as the full value of consideration less the cost of acquisition, cost of improvement and expenditure on transfer. The result is short-term or long-term by holding period. Exemptions require the reinvestment the exemption section states. A loss is set off only as the set-off section allows.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Computation comes before exemption. An exemption is lost if the new asset is not acquired as required.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 48 is the computation. Indexation and the cost of an acquisition by specified modes are computation rules. Sections 54, 54F and 54EC are exemptions with different assets and time limits. A short-term loss and a long-term loss do not set off against every head. The set-off section distinguishes them.
examples: A house is sold and the gain is computed under section 48.
A new house is bought within the exemption period.
A long-term loss is not set off against salary.
enhancement.problemApplication: Compute the gain, classify it, then apply exemption or set-off. Do not skip the transfer.
